simple.meaning: עָמֵק (ʻâmêq) is a Hebrew object word meaning “deep (literally or figuratively).” BibleIQ follows the concrete thing through the verses where it appears.
simple.biblicalBackground: The occurrence trail begins at Proverbs 9:18. The surrounding context includes Israel.
simple.inThisVerse: In this verse, the tapped English word is source-aligned to עָמֵק (H6012) in the Hebrew text.
simple.whyItMatters: Concrete words often carry patterns through Scripture because objects, animals, offerings, and created things are used repeatedly in worship, judgment, covenant, and narrative.
simple.summary: עָמֵק (ʻâmêq) / H6012 is traced through Proverbs 9:18, Isaiah 33:19, Ezekiel 3:5, Ezekiel 3:6 with generated occurrence evidence.

definitions.full: H6012. ameq [ עָמֵק ] adjective deep, unfathomable ; — plural construct שָׂפָה עִמְקֵי (Ges § 93ii ) i.e. unintelligible of speech Isa 33:19 ; Ezek 3:5-6 ,. — Prov 9:18 see עֹמֶק .

occurrences.englishText: But he doesn’t know that the departed spirits are there,
You will no longer see the fierce people,
For you are not sent to a people of a strange speech and of a hard language, but to the house of Israel;
not to many peoples of a strange speech and of a hard language, whose words you can’t understand. Surely, if I sent you to them, they would listen to you.
